LESSON: SIGN READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: PLOT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Plot
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Plot, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we know the key events in a play?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the sequence of events in a play,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Plot in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. assign signs to key events in a play,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Plot in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate the events in a play to real life experiences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Plot in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of a plot in a literary work. • Individually, learner is guided to sign read a play. • In groups, learners are guided to identify the key events in a play. • In groups, learners are guided to list, fingerspell and sign the key events identified. • In groups, learners are guided to role- play a section of a play. • In pairs, learners are guided to analyse the events in a play. • In groups, learners are guided to answer questions based on the plot. • In groups, learners are guided to create a summary of the key events and present it for peer assessment. • In pairs, learners are guided to make connections between events in a play and real life. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Plot together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn : Learner reflects on own work as he/she analyses and writes a summary of the events in a play

• Communication and collaboration: Learner develops the skill of teamwork as he/she interacts with others in groups

Values:
Unity: as the learner collaborates with peers to analyse the events in a play

Link to other subjects:

Drama and plays are studied in Kiswahili and Creative Arts.

Suggested Learning Resources:
